svg.title: Two parental sets establish the diploid zygote
svg.desc: One large cell boundary contains two separate pronuclei labelled23 maternal and23 paternal chromosomes. The depicted usual human stage is after completion of maternal meiosis II and before the next DNA-copying step. Together the sets establish46 chromosomes and diploidy; pronuclei are not drawn as already fused. Activation and cortical granule release change the coat to reduce further sperm interaction and help limit polyspermy. The figure does not portray a sea-urchin electrical fast block as the human mechanism. Later DNA replication precedes first mitosis without adding another parental set.

text.tspan: Two parental sets establish the diploid zygote
Usual human chromosome model after completion of maternal meiosis II.
Diploid zygote: two sets within one cell
Activation → cortical granule release → changes in the surrounding coat
These changes reduce additional sperm interaction and help limit polyspermy.
DNA is copied before the first mitosis; copying does not add another parental set.
Numbers are chromosome counts, not a drawing of every chromosome.
